recentItems.title: The end of ABC ME, and how Australia gave up on kids’ TV
recentItems.description:
In June 2024, Australia's largest dedicated kids' TV channel, ABC ME, was shut down in favor of launching two new entertainment channels, with shows from the former channel being split between these new channels and the ABC's on-demand service. How can this happen when Australia's own Bluey is one of the biggest shows in kids' TV? The closure of ABC ME is actually only part of the story, as Australia's childrens television production industry has been torn apart by weakened regulation and broadcaster disinterest. I explore the history of how Australia became such a powerhouse in international kids' TV, and explore the attitudes and actions that now look set to destroy that status, and how what's happening in Australia paints a grim picture also bodes poorly for the entire children's genre around the world.

For more on international kids' TV channels and the impacts they have, watch my video looking back at the closure of CITV in the UK: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W5pSY1ZG7pQ

recentItems.title: There’s still nothing new on Cartoon Network (2024 new shows commentary)
recentItems.description:

Why is CN relying on reboots and spinoffs for its new content, after so many years of not making much at all? Is it a viable strategy for them, given the perilous position they're already in? recentItems.title: Does The Fairly OddParents: A New Wish have any reason to exist? (review)
recentItems.description:

In a time where reboots and revivals seem more unjustifiably outlandish by the minute -- and this franchise is fresh off its own failed spinoff -- can Hazel's adventures find any reason to exist beside lining executive pockets? I review the show's first episodes, exploring the history of the franchise, the development of the series, and how it executes its story, plot, and creative direction. I also explore whether the show can make a name for itself beyond being just another reboot.

recentItems.title: How to handle the Dan Schneider allegations (”Quiet on Set” documentary commentary)
recentItems.description:
One of the biggest, most pervasive scandals in kids' TV is set to be exposed, as the new documentary series "Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids' TV" on Investigation Discovery explores the dark secrets surrounding the shows of Dan Schneider over his decades of domination at Nickelodeon. But as we all publicly reckon with the allegations and accusations of what happened behind the scenes at Schneider's Bakery, how do we, as viewers, respond to the controversy? I offer four big things to keep in mind as you watch the docuseries and navigate the weeks to come as social media and the kids' TV community at large grapples with the shocking new revelations. I also offer a few thoughts of my own on the Schneider situation, and how I've handled the topic in the past and going forward.

This is covering something a little different than my usual. For more of my typical story-focused, creatively-driven commentary, watch my recent look at the series finale of Danger Force, and how it ends a decade of kids' TV legacy in an underwhelming way: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W39x2D5NY-A

So why does "The Battle for Swellview" and the end of the Dangerverse feel so anticlimactic compared to the Henry Danger finale four years ago?
